title: Logarithmic Las Vegas dynamic connectivity
formal:
Do there exist a real constant \(K>0\), integers \(a\ge4\) and \(c\ge0\), and one uniform randomized online word-RAM data structure \(A\) with the following guarantees for every \(n\ge1\)?

Starting with the empty undirected simple graph on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), it processes every finite valid operation sequence \(\sigma\), fixed independently of its randomness, consisting of edge insertions, edge deletions and connectivity queries. It is always correct, all operations terminate almost surely, and, writing \(u\) and \(q\) for the numbers of updates and queries and \(\lambda_n=\log_2(n+2)\),
\[
 \mathbb E[T_A(n,\sigma)]\le
 K\bigl(n\lambda_n^c+(u+q)\lambda_n\bigr).
\]
Every individual query uses at most \(K\lambda_n\) instructions on every execution. The structure uses at most \(K(n+m)\lambda_n^c\) words when the current graph has \(m\) edges, with workspace counted as specified below. Its word length is \(w=a\lceil\lambda_n\rceil\).
definitions:
An insertion \(\operatorname{Insert}(v,z)\) adds one absent edge \(\{v,z\}\), with distinct endpoints in \([n]\). A deletion \(\operatorname{Delete}(v,z)\) removes one present edge. Loops and parallel edges are excluded. A query \(\operatorname{Connected}(v,z)\) returns one Boolean value indicating whether a finite path connects its endpoints in the current graph. A path of length zero is allowed, so \(\operatorname{Connected}(v,v)\) is true. No assumptions are made about degrees, components, planarity or update order.

Operations are supplied one at a time and answered before the next operation is supplied. The algorithm knows \(n\) at initialization but has no advance access to future operations or to their total number. The guarantee holds for every finite valid sequence and every prefix of that sequence, with no polynomial upper bound on sequence length. The sequence is chosen independently of the internal random words: this is an oblivious adversary. Access to hidden random state, response times or an exposed spanning forest is not supplied to the chooser. No public spanning forest is required as output.

The variable \(T_A(n,\sigma)\) counts initialization and all instructions used to process the sequence, including query and update outputs. The expectation is over independent uniform random words generated by the data structure. Every answer produced must be exact, not merely correct with high probability. Updates may have random unbounded running time on exceptional random tapes, but terminate almost surely; the displayed finite expectation is required for every finite sequence. Queries obey their deterministic instruction bound whenever invoked from a reachable state. The empty sequence imposes the stated expected initialization bound. Amortization permits an individual update to cost more than a logarithm.

Space is the total number of live stored words, including the graph representation, tables, copies, counters and temporary workspace, on every execution. Between operations, \(m\) is the current edge count. During one update, the bound uses the larger of the edge counts immediately before and after that update; these differ by one. During a query it uses the unchanged count, and during initialization it uses zero. Released storage cannot retain information accessible to the program without being counted. Space is not measured by a maximum edge count from the distant past.

The uniform sequential word RAM is a fixed finite program with unsigned \(w\)-bit registers and word-addressed memory, with no advice, oracle or free precomputed tables. Its unit-cost operations are reads, writes, copies, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, logical shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), and integer quotient and remainder by a nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Addresses and stored values fit words. Multiword computations pay for each constituent instruction. Generating an independent uniform random word costs one instruction. All initialization, table construction, memory management, auxiliary computation and output are charged. The same program and constants \(K,a,c\) work for every \(n\) and sequence.
why: Determine the logarithmic endpoint for a basic graph property under arbitrary edge insertions and deletions. It would close the remaining update-time gap to general information-access lower bounds under a precise, always-correct randomized guarantee.

context_blocks.text: An edge deletion can split a component, so fast insertion alone does not solve fully dynamic connectivity. The structure must detect whether another path still connects the endpoints.

The 2023 theorem achieves \(O(\log n(\log\log n)^2)\) amortized expected update time with always-correct answers. The target removes the factor \((\log\log n)^2\); it does not demand a worst-case bound for each update.

General cell-probe lower bounds already give a logarithmic obstruction for dynamic connectivity and tradeoffs between update and query costs. They motivate the endpoint without proving an additional superlogarithmic update requirement.

The SODA 2026 result guarantees a polylogarithmic expected bound for each update, a stronger temporal guarantee than amortization. Its unspecified polylogarithmic exponent does not give the particular logarithmic bound requested here.
Both cited upper-bound papers tolerate adversaries stronger than the fixed-sequence adversary in this card. That robustness is useful progress but is not an extra requirement on a solution here.

progress.text: Logarithmic randomized amortized cell-probe lower bounds and update/query tradeoffs establish a natural benchmark.
The full Las Vegas algorithm gives logarithmic updates times a squared iterated logarithm.
The SODA result gives polylogarithmic expected worst-case updates, addressing a different guarantee.

answer_criterion:
Give a complete Lean-checked proof that such a data structure and constants exist, or a complete Lean-checked proof of their logical nonexistence with the same online model, space bound and correctness and cost quantifiers.

A larger polylogarithmic update bound, a guarantee allowing erroneous answers, an offline algorithm or a special graph class does not establish the proposition. A lower bound on deterministic algorithms, worst-case updates or a stronger adversary does not by itself refute this Las Vegas amortized target. A conditional hardness result proves only its conditional conclusion. No numerical approximation tolerance applies.
status_note: Bounded primary-source checks through 17 September 2026 found no verified logarithmic amortized expected Las Vegas solution with the stated query and space guarantees, or unconditional impossibility result. The SODA 2026 expected worst-case theorem is polylogarithmic and does not state the logarithmic endpoint. Cited complete proofs were not independently audited.

source_formulation.text: The 2023 Las Vegas dynamic-connectivity result has amortized expected update time O(log n (log log n)^2) and logarithmic-or-smaller worst-case query time. This card asks whether the remaining squared iterated-logarithm update overhead can be removed while retaining exact answers and near-linear space.

checked_sources: Read Huang–Huang–Kopelowitz–Pettie–Thorup, TheoretiCS 2 Article 6, published 28 April 2023: Introduction pp. 1–3, Theorem 1.1, word-RAM model p. 6 and concluding discussion Section 11. It gives Las Vegas O(log n (log log n)^2) amortized expected updates and O(log n / log log log n) worst-case queries, even against a stronger adversary with internal-state access. The fixed target here retains the weaker oblivious-adversary requirement.

Read the primary author-hosted abstract of Patrascu–Demaine, SIAM Journal on Computing 35(4), 2006, pp. 932–963. It states an amortized randomized logarithmic cell-probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity, already on disjoint paths, and query/update tradeoffs. The page was updated in August 2026; that is not a new theorem date.

Read Meierhans–Probst Gutenberg, arXiv:2510.08297v1, 9 October 2025, SODA 2026: abstract, Introduction pp. 1–3 and Theorem 1.1. Its Las Vegas expected worst-case update guarantee is polylogarithmic, without the logarithmic exponent-one bound requested here. It handles a stronger adversary; this difference does not remove the quantitative gap. Only v1 was listed in the live history on the review date.

Bounded primary-source searches through 2026-09-17, including the authors’ publication pages and recent dynamic-connectivity results, did not locate a verified resolution of the precise logarithmic target. No full proof audit of the cited algorithms is claimed.
